lang: Hebrew (English summary p. 197* included in the PDF)
location_note: 'Ein el-Luza, c. 350 m south of the confluence of the Hinnom and Kidron Valleys, lower slopes of the Deir Abu Tor hill; Hebrew text map ref. NIG 2228/6302, OIG 1728/1302. The English summary prints NIG 22280/61302, OIG 17280/11302, which as written falls about 17 km further south and conflicts with the Hebrew text and the description; the Hebrew reference is used (choice C6).
notes: Three caves: natural Caves 1 and 3 with Iron II pottery and human bone fragments (burial use possible but problematic, or a dumped fill from an evacuated burial cave); Cave 2 a hewn Early Roman burial cave, recorded but not excavated.

features.subtype: natural cave with Iron II pottery, disturbed human bones and a few Hasmonean/Early Roman vessels; burial use or dumped fill (excavator)
features.period: Iron II (8th-early 6th c. BCE, some 10th-9th c.); in use in the Second Temple period (Hasmonean/Early Roman vessels)
features.quote: the cave had been in use in the Second Temple period

features.subtype: natural cave with Iron II pottery and human bone fragments
features.quote: are natural caves containing Iron II pottery and human bone fragments

features.subtype: hewn burial cave with skulls and bones
features.quote: is a hewn burial cave from the Early Roman period
